"'''Before the Next Teardrop Falls'''" is an American [[Country music|country]] song written by Vivian Keith and [[Ben Peters]], and most famously recorded by [[Freddy Fender]]. His version was a major crossover success in 1975, reaching number 1 on the ''[[Billboard (magazine)|Billboard]]'' pop and country charts. In 2025, the single was selected by the [[Library of Congress]] for preservation in the [[National Recording Registry]].<ref>{{cite web |title=National Recording Registry Inducts Sounds of Elton John, Chicago, Broadway's 'Hamilton,' Mary J. "Before the Next Teardrop Falls" is an American country song written by Vivian Keith and Ben Peters, and most famously recorded by Freddy Fender. His version was a major crossover success in 1975, reaching number 1 on the Billboard pop and country charts. In 2025, the single was selected by the Library of Congress for preservation in the National Recording Registry.

sections.heading: Song history
sections.wikitext:
The song was written in 1967 and had been recorded more than two dozen times. It had achieved modest success in versions by various performers; the original by [[Duane Dee]] reached number 44 on the ''Billboard'' country chart in early 1968, and [[Linda Martell]] sent her version to number 33 in early 1970. [[Jerry Lee Lewis]] included it on his 1969 album, ''[[Another Place, Another Time (album)|Another Place Another Time]]''.<ref>{{cite web|author=Stephen Thomas Erlewine|author-link=Stephen Thomas Erlewine|url=http://www.allmusic.com/album/another-place-another-time-mw0000847835 |title=Another Place Another Time - Jerry Lee Lewis | Songs, Reviews, Credits |publisher=[[AllMusic]] |access-date=2015-11-12}}</ref>

In 1974, record producer [[Huey P. Meaux]] approached Fender about overdubbing vocals for an instrumental track. Fender agreed, performing the song bilingual style—singing the first half of the song in English, then repeating it in Spanish. "The recording only took a few minutes", Fender told an interviewer, "I was glad to get it over with and I thought that would be the last of it".<ref>{{cite web|first=Bill |last=Janovitz |url=http://www.allmusic.com/song/before-the-next-teardrop-falls-mt0006417796 |title=Before the Next Teardrop Falls - Freddy Fender | Song Info |publisher=[[AllMusic]] |access-date=2015-11-12}}</ref>

The single was first released on Meaux's Crazy Cajun label in 1974, but was soon picked up for wider distribution by [[Dot Records|ABC-Dot]]. "Before the Next Teardrop Falls" immediately took off in popularity when released to country radio in January 1975. The song ascended to number 1 on the ''[[Billboard (magazine)|Billboard]]'' [[Hot Country Songs|Hot Country Singles]] chart in March, spending two weeks atop the chart.<ref>{{cite book |title= The Billboard Book Of Top 40 Country Hits: 1944-2006, Second edition|last=Whitburn |first=Joel |author-link=Joel Whitburn |year=2004 |publisher=Record Research |page=120}}</ref> Thereafter, the song caught on just as strongly at [[contemporary hit radio|top 40]] radio stations and it was not long before Fender had a number 1 [[Billboard Hot 100|''Billboard'' Hot 100]] hit as well. ''Billboard'' ranked it as the [[Billboard Year-End Hot 100 singles of 1975|number four song of 1975]].

As originally composed, it is in [[thirty-two-bar form|32-bar form]] (Fender's bilingual recording stretches the piece to 48 bars).

A showcase of Fender's [[tenor]] and Meaux's Tex-Mex musical styling, "Before the Next Teardrop Falls" jump-started his career. (Fender's career had stalled in 1960 after his arrest on drug charges.)<ref>Tucker, Stephen R., "Freddy Fender", ''The Encyclopedia of Country Music'', Paul Kingsbury, ed. New York: [[Oxford University Press]], 1998, {{ISBN|978-0195176087}}.</ref> In the months and years that followed, Fender recorded several bilingual standards which became major hits, most notably "[[Secret Love (1953 song)|Secret Love]]".

Fender also recorded a version fully in Spanish, entitled "Estaré contigo cuando triste estés"<ref>Archived at [https://ghostarchive.org/varchive/youtube/20211205/ir6Dfgt9e7I Ghostarchive]{{cbignore}} and the [https://web.archive.org/web/20180514143346/https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ir6Dfgt9e7I&gl=US&hl=en Wayback Machine]{{cbignore}}: {{cite web| url = https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ir6Dfgt9e7I| title = Freddy Fender - Estare contigo cuando triste estas (Before the Next Tear drop Falls Espanol) .mp4 | website=[[YouTube]]| date = 6 July 2011 }}{{cbignore}}</ref> (literally "I will be with you when you are sad"). The Spanish-language second verse in the English version is the first verse of the fully Spanish version.
sections.text:
The song was written in 1967 and had been recorded more than two dozen times. It had achieved modest success in versions by various performers; the original by Duane Dee reached number 44 on the Billboard country chart in early 1968, and Linda Martell sent her version to number 33 in early 1970. Jerry Lee Lewis included it on his 1969 album, Another Place Another Time.

In 1974, record producer Huey P. Meaux approached Fender about overdubbing vocals for an instrumental track. Fender agreed, performing the song bilingual style—singing the first half of the song in English, then repeating it in Spanish. "The recording only took a few minutes", Fender told an interviewer, "I was glad to get it over with and I thought that would be the last of it".

The single was first released on Meaux's Crazy Cajun label in 1974, but was soon picked up for wider distribution by ABC-Dot. "Before the Next Teardrop Falls" immediately took off in popularity when released to country radio in January 1975. The song ascended to number 1 on the Billboard Hot Country Singles chart in March, spending two weeks atop the chart. Thereafter, the song caught on just as strongly at top 40 radio stations and it was not long before Fender had a number 1 Billboard Hot 100 hit as well. Billboard ranked it as the number four song of 1975.

As originally composed, it is in 32-bar form (Fender's bilingual recording stretches the piece to 48 bars).

A showcase of Fender's tenor and Meaux's Tex-Mex musical styling, "Before the Next Teardrop Falls" jump-started his career. (Fender's career had stalled in 1960 after his arrest on drug charges.) In the months and years that followed, Fender recorded several bilingual standards which became major hits, most notably "Secret Love".

Fender also recorded a version fully in Spanish, entitled "Estaré contigo cuando triste estés" (literally "I will be with you when you are sad"). The Spanish-language second verse in the English version is the first verse of the fully Spanish version.

sections.heading: Successes
sections.wikitext:
"Before the Next Teardrop Falls" was certified gold for sales of one million units by the [[Recording Industry Association of America]].<ref>[https://www.riaa.com/gp/database/search_results.asp] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20070608063940/http://www.riaa.com/gp/database/search_results.asp|date=June 8, 2007}}</ref> It also won the Single of the Year award from the [[Country Music Association]] in 1975, and was conducive to Fender also winning that year's Album of the Year and Male Vocalist of the Year awards.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.cmaawards.com/2007/database/ArtistDetail.aspx?artistId=167 |title=Homepage - 2015 CMA Awards |publisher=Cmaawards.com |access-date=2015-11-12 }}{{Dead link|date=June 2020 |bot=InternetArchiveBot |fix-attempted=yes }}</ref>

The song was used in the movies ''[[Something Wild (1986 film)|Something Wild]]'' (1986) and ''[[The Three Burials of Melquiades Estrada]]'' (2005).
sections.text:
"Before the Next Teardrop Falls" was certified gold for sales of one million units by the Recording Industry Association of America. It also won the Single of the Year award from the Country Music Association in 1975, and was conducive to Fender also winning that year's Album of the Year and Male Vocalist of the Year awards.

The song was used in the movies Something Wild (1986) and The Three Burials of Melquiades Estrada (2005).

sections.heading: 1975 country-pop "half-dozen"
sections.wikitext: "Before the Next Teardrop Falls" was one of six songs released in 1975 that topped both the ''Billboard'' Hot 100 and ''Billboard'' Hot Country Singles charts. The others were "[[(Hey Won't You Play) Another Somebody Done Somebody Wrong Song]]" by [[B. J. Thomas]]; "[[Rhinestone Cowboy]]" by [[Glen Campbell]]; "[[Thank God I'm a Country Boy]]" and the two-sided hit "[[I'm Sorry (John Denver song)|I'm Sorry]]"/"[[Calypso (John Denver song)|Calypso]]" by [[John Denver]]; and "[[Convoy (song)|Convoy]]" by [[C. W. McCall]].
sections.text: "Before the Next Teardrop Falls" was one of six songs released in 1975 that topped both the Billboard Hot 100 and Billboard Hot Country Singles charts. The others were "(Hey Won't You Play) Another Somebody Done Somebody Wrong Song" by B. J. Thomas; "Rhinestone Cowboy" by Glen Campbell; "Thank God I'm a Country Boy" and the two-sided hit "I'm Sorry"/"Calypso" by John Denver; and "Convoy" by C. W. McCall.

sections.heading: Covers
sections.wikitext:
* [[Charley Pride]] included the song in his 1968 album ''[[Make Mine Country]]''.
* [[Gene Stuart]] went to number 3 with it in the [[Irish Recorded Music Association|IRMA Irish charts]] in 1969.
* [[Loretta Lynn]] recorded it for her album ''[[Home (Loretta Lynn album)|Home]]'' in 1975.
* Mexican singer [[Angelica Maria]] covered the song in an album of the same name in 1975.
* [[Lee Dorsey]], on the album ''Am I That Easy to Forget?,'' a posthumous release in 1987.
* Cantonese version of the song, called 流下眼淚前, performed by Hong Kong singer [[Paula Tsui]] in 1987.
* [[Dolly Parton]] included it on her 1996 covers album ''[[Treasures (Dolly Parton album)|Treasures]]''; Parton's version featured vocals by [[David Hidalgo]], who sang the Spanish lyrics.
* Clay Walker also recorded his version but along with Freddy Fender on his album Fall in 2007.
* Regional Mexican singer [[Jenni Rivera]] recorded two versions (English and Spanish) for her eleventh studio album ''[[La Gran Señora]],'' released on December 1, 2009.
* [[Al Green]] recorded the song in 2018 for the Amazon Music "Produced By" series.
* [[The Mavericks]] included it on their 2019 ''Play the Hits'' release of favorite covers.
* [[Liza Colón-Zayas]]'s character [[Tina Marrero]] sang the song at a karaoke bar in an episode of [[The Bear season 2|''The Bear'' season two]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://ew.com/the-bear-star-liza-colon-zayas-freaked-out-season-2-episode-5-pop-tina-sings-8658372|title=Why 'The Bear' star Liza Colón-Zayas 'freaked out' about filming Tina's big moment|website=EW.com}}</ref>  
* [[Me First and the Gimme Gimmes]] on the album ¡Blow it...at Madison's Quinceañera! in 2024.
